engagement_title: Corner & Cure counter refit: bring a phone shot food archive to one warm counter look, recover the hand painted board sign as artwork a vinyl cutter can actually use, and build the window, the wall board, the cold case labels and the daily posts off it
vertical: Food, hospitality and travel, a fast casual neighbourhood deli counter with a marketplace storefront, Brooklyn, New York
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post from a scrappy New York style sandwich shop needing storefront art for a delivery ordering app, asking for something 'gritty, bold, and a little chaotic', 'not polished or corporate', and saying 'we have the assets, they just need to be pulled together so they look like they were shot in the same image'. The real shop is named in the post, so it is laundered to the coined fictional Corner & Cure and the marketplace is genericised. Co-anchors: the Upwork post from a family owned neighbourhood restaurant wanting static paid social creative for two recurring offers, personality stated as 'authentic, community-focused, family-oriented, warm, bold, local neighborhood favorite' and explicitly not a corporate chain, laundered to a fictional operator; and the Freelancer.com post for a fast food counter wanting a 'creative, vibrant, and appetizing' menu in a 'retro, street-food, rustic chalkboard' style with room for photography and print ready output. The ledger's verdict is REBUILD because the original concept sat almost entirely on one authoring surface. The honest fuller commission is what all three clients are really buying: one warm counter look pulled out of their own phone pictures, their own hand painted sign recovered as artwork rather than redrawn, and that material carried onto the window, the wall, the cold case and the daily posts.
client_one_liner: Everything we have was shot on a phone over the counter, the only version of our sign is painted on a board screwed to the wall, and the window guy, the label printer and the ordering app all want files from us this month.
client_brief:
Corner & Cure, counter refit

We are a deli on a corner in Brooklyn. Sandwiches, bowls, a cold case, a coffee machine, twelve to sixteen dollars, people who work nearby and come in three times a week. My father opened it and I run it now. We are refitting the front of house and every piece of paper and vinyl in the place is being replaced at once.

Our pictures. Everything we have was shot on my phone, over the counter, on the paper we wrap on, while people were waiting. There are a lot of them and they are all a bit different: some at lunch with the door open, some at four in the afternoon with just the strip light. We want them to look like one shop. Warm, loud, food up close and looking like you want to eat it now, not like a magazine.

Our sign. The name is painted on a board over the slicer. My father had it done by a sign painter twenty years ago and there is no file anywhere. The window company needs artwork they can cut vinyl from, not a photograph, and it goes on the glass at about a hand's width tall across the middle of the window. It has to still be our sign.

What we need. The board on the wall behind the counter, laid out in tiles so we can swap one when a special changes. A big poster for the window. The daily special posts, in the three shapes the platforms want, in one file we can open ourselves. A small card by the register with our hours and the loyalty thing. Labels for the cold case, one per item, printed off our item list, because the printer wants a run of them. And enough of a written basis that the next person we hire does not repaint the whole thing.

We are not fancy and we do not want to look it. But we are not cheap either, and cheap is what this stuff usually looks like.
price_band_and_audience: Twelve to sixteen dollars for a sandwich or a bowl, walk up neighbourhood trade, mostly twenty to forty five, three visits a week, decided in about eight seconds at the counter or six on a phone. The band is load bearing. At impulse pricing the food is shown warm, saturated and cropped close enough to read across a room, the boards are dense but scannable, the price is set at tile size in the display face because the price is the offer, and the whole thing carries the hand of the painted sign rather than a neutral grid. Treat the same photographs the way the sibling tasting room commission is correctly treated, dark grounds, one dish a page, price whispered at body size, and a twelve dollar sandwich shop reads as pretentious and empty. Push the other way into starbursts and four fonts and it reads as a franchise nobody trusts with a sandwich. A posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Sandwiches worth leaving the block for.
brand_identity.sector: A fast casual neighbourhood deli counter with a cold case and a marketplace storefront, on a corner in Brooklyn, New York.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opened by the current owner's father, now run by his son, Brooklyn, New York. A single corner shop refitting its whole front of house at once.
brand_identity.about: Corner & Cure is a corner deli: sandwiches, bowls, a cold case and a coffee machine, for the people who work nearby and come in three times a week. It is loud, warm and unpretentious, run by the family that opened it. The food is made to be wanted right now, not admired later.
brand_identity.audience: Walk up trade, mostly twenty to forty five, three visits a week, deciding in about eight seconds at the counter or six on a phone. They want appetite and honesty, not polish.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve to sixteen dollars for a sandwich or a bowl. Impulse priced but not cheap: the price is the offer and sits large and proud, while the whole shop works to look like a place that is worth it rather than a bargain or a franchise.
brand_identity.typography: The hand painted board sign carries the name and sets the tone. Around it, a bold condensed display face for the wall board, prices and specials, prices at tile size so they read across the room, with a plain workhorse sans for hours, loyalty rules and small print. Warm and loud, never a novelty pile.
brand_identity.voice: Plainspoken, neighbourhood, a little brash and generous. Example line the brand would write: 'Pulled together, piled high, see you at the counter.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no digital version of the sign: the name survives only as a board hand painted by a sign painter twenty years ago and screwed to the wall over the slicer. Everything else was shot on the owner's phone over the counter. A two page written note holds the voice, hours, loyalty rules and section names, and the label printer holds a press file.
brand_identity.values: A family corner shop, second generation. Real food for regulars, made with the hand of a place, not a chain.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_counter_shots/ (18 phone frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photography shot by the owner over the counter across several weeks, food on the shop's own butcher paper, mixed daylight and strip light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we have. Shot on my phone on the paper we wrap on. Some at lunch, some late afternoon."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The butcher paper sits at almost the same value as a toasted crust, so on an unknown subset of frames a one call knockout returns a clean looking complete cutout that has quietly bitten the crust edge where the two meet, and the bite is invisible until the cutout is placed on the marketplace's flat ground. The frames are also phone scale, so nothing cut from them can carry a large format window piece, and three of the eighteen are the same sandwich shot on three different days.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_board_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the hand painted name board over the slicer, shot at an angle under tungsten: brush drawn letters with hairline joins, plus a small painted knife device beside the word.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only version of our sign. My father had it painted twenty years ago and there is no file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The painted letterforms carry hairline brush joins and small counters that a trace holds comfortably at full canvas and closes at the height the window actually reproduces the mark, on the actual glass colour rather than on white. It is also a compound lockup, so a selection naming the whole sign returns the word and silently drops the knife device, and paint and aged board run close in value across the shadowed half of the board.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_label_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press file the label printer supplied for the cold case shelf label: a small landscape label carrying an item name, a size line, a price roundel and a dietary tag strip.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The label our printer already runs. This is his file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed label reads as four separate blocks with a picture well in the roundel, but the roundel is a decorative element rather than a picture frame and the name, size and price were set as one continuous flow, so the frame inventory the conversion exposes is nothing like the printed label suggests. The file carries no bleed, so a press ready delivery with bleed cannot be honoured from it.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_items.csv (38 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The cold case item list: item name, size, price, dietary tags and a picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything in the case. This is the list we print off."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three items were never photographed and their picture cells are simply blank, which no header reveals and which the merge will not complain about. Prices are written inconsistently across rows, and two items share a name at two different sizes, so naming one file per item by name collides and silently overwrites.

assets_supplied.name: cornerandcure_brand_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Two pages the owner wrote: the voice, the hours, the loyalty rules, the section names for the wall board and a note that the specials change daily.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk and what goes where. The specials change every day, so we have to be able to swap them."

acceptance_bar: The eighteen phone frames read as one shop across the wall board, the window and the posts: one warmth, one black point, one sense of how close the food sits. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.

Every marketplace item tile sits on the flat brand ground at the marketplace's tile size with clear air at every edge, and the cut edge holds where the food meets the wrapping paper when looked at close up rather than at thumbnail scale.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry. Anything printing larger than a phone frame supports comes from a source that can carry it.

The sign is placeable cutting artwork rather than a picture of a sign: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, the knife device present alongside the word, and every counter still open at the height it actually goes on the glass, on the glass colour rather than on white.

The wall board is laid out as tiles that can be swapped one at a time without relaying the board, and every text object is live editable text in one licensed type system with family and real weight declared on the element.
The three social canvases sit in one working document, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source they were built from.
Prices are set at tile size in the display face and read across the room, and the whole system carries the hand of the painted sign rather than a neutral grid.

The cold case run produces one label per item with the right item's own price and tags, page count equalling row count, per item files identifiable where two items share a name, and the three items with no picture handled deliberately rather than left as holes.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that the supplied print file cannot carry, and the shortfall is reported.

The note records per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the real numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, the sign recovery and its safe minimum height, and everything that could not be delivered.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted here and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision and the sign recovery. It fixes one warm counter target off the best lit frame and brings each of the eighteen toward it one call at a time across two lighting conditions, triages the knockout route per frame between the one call route and a material named selection of the wrapping paper inverted and filled, cuts the marketplace tiles and the label pictures, and recovers the painted sign at ink level with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt including its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution
adobe_surfaces.role: The cold case label run, the only genuine one record per page job here. The label printer's press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, offsets computed from the document's own reconstructed story text rather than the mapping readout, the graded item pictures bound per row through a prefixed picture column, and the run has to reach the counter staff as proofs whose identity is actually trustworthy.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express by url, asset_search with entityScope CCAsset, asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The four pieces the shop maintains itself: the swappable tile wall board, the window poster at a true physical size, the register card, and three daily special canvases at three sizes in one export. Photographs are carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the recovered sign goes in as inline vector so it stays editable, and the returned per canvas markup is the only place the importer reports what it changed.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend called once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across the board, poster, register card and posts, sitting beside a hand painted sign without competing with it. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on warm and loud without becoming a novelty pile. Numeric weights are non standard per family and one unlaunderable name kills the entire kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search with entityScope StockAsset, a short query, a contentType filter and never orientation, asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the shop cannot supply, a camera scale counter or street frame large enough to carry the window poster, IP clean, generative candidates excluded, then graded into the same warm target so it does not read as bought beside the phone pictures. The Boards half persists the selects the owner signs off from, with a partial result read as partial and vector understood to be unboardable.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, settle which deliverable lands on which surface, and upload every asset holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: The board, poster, register card and posts are collateral the shop edits itself, which only the authoring surface composes; the cold case labels are one record per page at volume, which only the merge surface does.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan, the confirmed tier, and a manifest keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at all eighteen counter frames and triage them: which lighting condition each belongs to, which are off level, how close the food sits, where food meets wrapping paper, and which item each actually shows against the thirty eight row list.
trajectory.judgement: The owner believes he has a picture of everything. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and reading eighteen frames against thirty eight rows is not counting files.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note plus the picture to item reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and phone frames have none to spare.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one warm counter target off the best lit frame and bring each of the eighteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eighteen appetising pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames split between open door daylight and a strip light, and at this band warmth is the brand rather than a correction.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the marketplace item tiles: knock each frame onto the flat brand ground at the marketplace's tile size with air at every edge, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff array is the only channel that reports what a tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. Optical centring on a stacked sandwich is not geometric centring.
trajectory.produces: Item tiles on the brand ground with their returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for the counter or street frame the window poster needs, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, then bring it to the warm target.
trajectory.judgement: Nothing cut from a phone frame can carry a large format window piece, so the poster hero has to come from a source that is genuinely camera scale. Choose the frame whose light can reach the target rather than the best thumbnail.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the set.

trajectory.action: Recover the painted sign: an ink level selection naming the paint's own visual properties rather than the board it sits on, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the board, a compound naming drops the knife device, background removal is the wrong instrument on painted letterforms with counters, and the tracer takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent sign plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a twelve to sixteen dollar counter and a hand painted sign it must sit beside without competing.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author the swappable tile wall board, the window poster at a true physical size, the register card and the three daily special canvases, each root declaring its own canvas, photographs carried as embedded image data, the recovered sign placed as inline vector inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored top left, family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is tile density, how large the price sits, and where the sign goes so a swapped special never touches it.
trajectory.produces: Export ready sources for all four documents, retained as durable deliverables.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export each document by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the rendition and look at the first canvas, and read the returned per canvas markup for everything after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every change this importer makes returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard.
trajectory.produces: Native editable documents, an inspected first canvas each, and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the label printer's press PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each holds.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed label looks like says nothing about how the file was set, and the picture well the printed sample implies may not be a picture frame at all. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory and a mapping strategy chosen from it.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the document's true story text from the interchange file, compute every offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened string and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re-exported document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection, not by a success message.

trajectory.action: Cut the label pictures from the graded masters to the label's proportion, reading what each crop reports about its confidence and bounds, and reconcile them against the item list including the rows that have nothing.
trajectory.judgement: A blank picture cell is not an error the merge will raise, so what a label with no photograph looks like is the agent's decision, made before the run rather than found on the printed sheet.
trajectory.produces: Label pictures per row with confidence recorded, and a stated treatment for the rows with none.

trajectory.action: Run the item list against the template binding each row's own picture, produce the printer's run and per item proofs for the counter staff, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: One picture repeated across every label is what a naive run ships, the naming key has to survive two items sharing a name, and a file's position in a returned list is not evidence of which record is inside it.
trajectory.produces: The cold case run plus per item proofs, each verified against its row.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries named as failed, then write the handover note and the brand basis.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success code, vector is not boardable so the sign belongs in the note, and the basis has to let the next hire swap a special without repainting the system.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, plus the written basis and handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut edge survives where the food meets the paper it is sitting on. The shop wraps on butcher paper and photographs on it, and on an unknown subset of frames the paper sits at almost the value of a toasted crust. The knockout reports success, the returned cutout is complete and clean at thumbnail scale, and the bite only exists along the short stretch where crust and paper share luminance. Which frames it happens to is a property of each photograph's own light, not of the sandwich, and there is no confidence figure and no edge report anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the edge quality is a fact about this frame meeting this tool and exists only after the call has run and the result has been looked at on the ground it will sit on, not on white. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the food was shot on the paper they wrap on. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain for the affected frames, a material named selection of the wrapping paper, inverted and filled to the brand ground.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route per frame, re-derive the affected tiles through the selection and fill chain, and re-inspect every tile against the marketplace's actual flat ground rather than against white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A marketplace storefront where the hero sandwiches have a chewed edge along the crust on the frames nobody looked at closely, on the one surface where a customer decides in six seconds.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered sign is still the sign at the height it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the word is there, the brush drawn letterforms are there, the counters are open, and at full canvas on a white page it is a faithful recovery. The window company puts it on the glass at about a hand's width tall across a dark painted band, and at that height on that ground the hairline brush joins fill in and the small counters close into solid blobs. The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on its real ground and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the ground colour being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the window. Nothing states it: the brief asks for artwork the window company can cut and says the mark has to still be their sign. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same tracer, a differently worded selection, a fill and flatten plate instead of a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees, since the tracer itself has no lever.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster on a different route, re-trace, re-inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re-place the result at reproduction height on the real ground and re-judge, and state a safe minimum height in the handover once one is actually known.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Vinyl cut and applied to the window in which the family name reads as a row of solid shapes, which is both the most visible piece in the refit and the one that cannot be quietly reprinted.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered label proof actually contains the record its filename claims. The natural way to give counter staff a proof per item is a multi record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number. The labels are wrong: the files come back in an order that does not match the roster, and nothing in the response says so. Every gate above it passes, the count is right, each file is a valid label, and the only way to find out is to open the files and read the item name and price inside them against the row they were named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mislabelling is in the response itself and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name the files. Nothing states it: the acceptance line about the right item's own price is the shop's requirement and the brief never characterises the delivery. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route, either a single multi page run whose page order is trustworthy or a per record run producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi record raster route, re-run the cold case set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, and re-check the two items that share a name so the collision does not silently overwrite.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A cold case where the price under the turkey is the price of the roast beef, printed, laminated and clipped into the rail, discovered by a customer rather than by the shop.

deliverables.name: Corner & Cure counter photography
deliverables.spec: Eighteen phone frames brought to one warm counter look, one warmth, one black point and one sense of how close the food sits, plus one licensed camera scale frame graded into the same world so it can carry the window piece. At or below source pixel dimensions, with a per frame parameter log and the picture to item reconciliation stated, including the items with no photograph.

deliverables.name: Marketplace item tile set
deliverables.spec: Item tiles knocked onto the flat brand ground at the marketplace's tile size, product optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds where food meets wrapping paper under close inspection rather than at thumbnail scale, with the returned resize record captured for each. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Recovered Corner & Cure sign
deliverables.spec: The hand painted board recovered as placeable scalable cutting artwork with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, the knife device present beside the word, delivered as a single colour cutting version and a colour accurate variant, holding its counters at the height it actually goes on the glass and on the glass colour, with a stated safe minimum height.

deliverables.name: Wall board, window poster, register card and daily special set
deliverables.spec: A tile wall board a special can be swapped into without relaying the board, a window poster at a true physical size, a register card carrying hours and loyalty rules, and three daily special canvases at three sizes inside one export each keeping its own canvas, all on one licensed type system with the recovered sign as real vector and every photograph carried as embedded data. Delivered with their sources.

deliverables.name: Cold case label run
deliverables.spec: The label printer's press file reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the item list: the printer's run with page count equal to row count in roster order, plus per item proofs named from what is actually inside them on a key that survives two items sharing a name, with the rows that have no picture handled deliberately.

deliverables.name: Brand basis and handover note
deliverables.spec: A short written basis covering the warm palette, the type roles with family, foundry or designer and the real numeric weight, the photo treatment rule and how to swap a special without breaking the board, plus a note recording per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs, every resize any tool reported, the sign recovery and its safe minimum height, the bleed reality of the supplied press file, and everything that could not be delivered.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered raster exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry.
verifiers_auto.how: For every delivered raster read its pixel dimensions from the file header and assert neither axis exceeds its source per the manifest (the eighteen phone frames and the board sign are 4032x3024; the one licensed Stock hero is 7360x4912); then diff every returned crop_and_resize tradeoffs object against the resize table in the handover note and assert no entry reports an output larger than its input on either axis.

verifiers_auto.text: Every marketplace item tile is exactly 1080 x 1080 px square and sits on a single flat brand ground colour at all four corners.
verifiers_auto.how: Read each tile's pixel dimensions and assert both axes are exactly 1080 (a 1:1 square well below the 4032x3024 source, so no enlargement); then sample a 32x32 px patch at each of the four corners and assert all four are one identical RGB value that matches one of the five brand palette hexes (#B4382C, #D9A536, #F2E7CE, #2A2622, #4E6B3A), confirming a flat brand ground rather than photographic content at the edges.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered sign's SVG has a viewBox attribute, no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero, and contains geometry for both the word and the knife device.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a numeric viewBox attribute is present, assert the element at path index zero is not an axis-aligned rectangle spanning the full viewBox (no opaque full-canvas ground path), and count the top-level path groups, asserting at least two distinct groups so both the word and the knife device carry geometry.

verifiers_auto.text: Each Express export returned exactly its declared canvas count with per-canvas pixel sizes equal to what its HTML root declared: wall board = 1 canvas, window poster = 1, register card = 1, daily specials = 3 canvases at 1080x1080, 1080x1350 and 1080x1920 px; and no image on any canvas resolved to the importer's 1x1 placeholder.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and each canvas's returned width and height from every export response and assert they equal those counts and sizes (the poster canvas equalling its declared physical size at exactly 96 dpi); then parse the returned per-canvas markup and assert no img or image element resolves to a 1x1 single-pixel placeholder data URI.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in every export carries a resolved licensed face rather than a fallback default, and the same two kit families appear across all four documents.

decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document the shop edits itself, and which is a genuine one record per page run at volume.
Whether the eighteen frames are one shop, and how far to push the strip light frames before they stop being worth saving.
Knockout route per frame, between the one call route and a material named selection of the wrapping paper inverted and filled, where food and paper share value.
Where the window poster hero comes from, given nothing cut from a phone frame can carry it and enlargement is not an option.
Selection wording on the painted board: naming the board takes the substrate, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and a compound naming silently drops the knife device.
Whether the single colour cutting version or the colour accurate variant is what the window company actually needs, judged at reproduction height on the glass colour.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an impulse band and a hand painted sign it must sit beside, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How dense the wall board can get before it stops being scannable across the room, and how large the price has to sit for the offer to survive at eight seconds.
What a label for an item with no photograph looks like, decided before the run rather than found on the printed sheet.
Which delivery route carries per record identity safely, and what key names a file when two items share a name.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns appetising pictures of sandwiches and a picture of a chalkboard. IDENTITY: these are this shop's own sandwiches on this shop's own paper, and the sign is a specific hand painted board a sign painter made twenty years ago, which has to be RECOVERED rather than reinvented, because a regenerated sign is a different family's name in a different hand and the window company cuts vinyl from paths, not from a picture. SPEC: the marketplace needs tiles at an exact size on a flat ground with a cut edge that survives close inspection, the window needs a closed path that still reads at a stated height, and the cold case needs one label per item bound to that item's own price with page count equal to row count, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the specials change daily and the shop swaps them itself, so a flat picture of a board is worthless a day after delivery. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout bite the crust, does this trace hold at hand height on green, is the price inside this file the price on this row.
